title: Cannabis Financial Access & Compliance Readiness Assessment v2

questions.question: Do legal entity names, trade names, ownership records, licenses, tax registrations, and banking records consistently identify the same operating structure?
questions.evidence: Entity documents, state licenses, EIN/tax records, bank account titles

questions.question: Is the current ownership list/cap table (or equivalent ownership record) accurate and complete, including direct and indirect owners, financial interests, control relationships, and identification of any person meeting Ohio's 10%-or-greater ownership disclosure threshold (O.A.C. 1301:18-3-04)?
questions.evidence: Ownership list and capitalization table, organizational chart, 10%+ owner certifications, change logs

questions.question: Before entering or completing ownership, financial-interest, control, entity-name, or trade-name changes, does the operator identify applicable DCC notice or prior-approval requirements (O.A.C. 1301:18-3-06 — prior approval required for ownership changes of 10% or more, aggregated per calendar year) and retain evidence of submission or approval?
questions.evidence: DCC change-of-ownership application, approval/notice correspondence, internal change-control log tracking aggregate ownership movement year-to-date

questions.question: Can the company document source of initial and material subsequent capital, loans, and investor funds?
questions.evidence: Subscription agreements, loan documents, wire records, investor files

questions.question: Is there a documented process to keep licenses, permits, registrations, and required ownership disclosures current?
questions.evidence: License calendar, renewal files, responsible owner, filing evidence

questions.question: Does each financial institution used by the company know the nature of the cannabis-related business and permit the relationship?
questions.evidence: Account agreements, onboarding correspondence, cannabis program documentation

questions.question: Are all operating, payroll, tax, merchant, lending, and investment accounts inventoried with clear ownership and authorized signers?
questions.evidence: Account inventory, signer list, treasury map

questions.question: Does the company have a process for responding promptly and consistently to bank due-diligence requests?
questions.evidence: CDD request log, document package, designated bank liaison

questions.question: Are bank-imposed conditions, deposit requirements, transaction restrictions, reporting requirements, and fees documented and monitored?
questions.evidence: Bank program terms, compliance calendar, exception log

questions.question: Is there a contingency plan for account closure, payment-service disruption, or loss of a key banking relationship?
questions.evidence: Business continuity plan, alternate banking strategy, escalation contacts

questions.question: Are cash receipts, drawers, vaults, transfers, deposits, and variances reconciled under documented procedures?
questions.evidence: Cash SOP, daily reconciliation, variance reports, deposit logs

questions.question: Are dual control, access restrictions, segregation of duties, and physical-security controls used for material cash movements?
questions.evidence: Vault access, permissions, dual-count records, camera/security procedures

questions.question: Are armored-car, cash-vault, merchant, ATM, ACH, debit, and other payment providers approved and monitored before use?
questions.evidence: Contracts, due diligence, fee/flow review, provider inventory

questions.question: Can the company trace material incoming and outgoing funds to a legitimate business purpose and supporting documentation?
questions.evidence: Invoices, contracts, purchase orders, payment approvals, GL support

questions.question: Are owners, control persons, material investors, lenders, and other high-risk counterparties identified and subject to risk-based due diligence?
questions.evidence: Identity documents, beneficial ownership, background checks, risk files

questions.question: Does the company have a risk-based process for sanctions screening of relevant owners, control persons, counterparties, and vendors?
questions.evidence: Screening procedure, vendor/tool output, escalation records

questions.question: Are financial-crime red flags documented for staff, including unusual payments, third-party funding, unexplained cash, structuring indicators, fraud, or identity concerns?
questions.evidence: Red-flag guide, SOP, training material, escalation examples

questions.question: Is there a documented internal escalation path for suspected fraud, illicit finance, sanctions concerns, identity issues, or suspicious counterparties?
questions.evidence: Escalation matrix, case log, decision records, responsible officer

questions.question: Can the company explain its business model, revenue sources, major counterparties, and expected transaction patterns in a way a bank can readily understand?
questions.evidence: Business narrative, flow-of-funds map, revenue analysis, counterparty profile

questions.question: Are material vendors and service providers subject to documented onboarding and risk-based due diligence?
questions.evidence: Vendor questionnaire, ownership/licensing checks, contract review

questions.question: Are high-risk vendors, management companies, consultants, payment intermediaries, and related parties identified for enhanced review?
questions.evidence: Risk tiering, related-party register, enhanced review records

questions.question: Do contracts give the company adequate documentation, audit, termination, compliance, and data-access rights for material providers?
questions.evidence: Vendor contracts, compliance clauses, audit/data rights

questions.question: Are inventory/seed-to-sale records, point-of-sale data, deposits, and general-ledger revenue periodically reconciled with documented exceptions?
questions.evidence: METRC/seed-to-sale reports, POS reports, physical inventory/cycle-count records, deposit records, GL reconciliation

questions.question: Are tax obligations, filings, payment deadlines, and tax-payment accounts assigned, documented, and monitored?
questions.evidence: Tax calendar, filing/payment evidence, responsible owner

questions.question: Are records needed for regulators, banks, auditors, tax authorities, and internal investigations retained in an organized and retrievable manner?
questions.evidence: Retention schedule, shared repository, access controls, retrieval test

questions.question: Is compliance responsibility assigned to a named person who has sufficient access, independence, and authority to stop or escalate activity that may violate law, license requirements, banking conditions, or internal policy?
questions.evidence: Job description/charter defining authority, escalation-without-retaliation policy, examples of exercised authority

questions.question: Do relevant employees receive documented training on cash controls, fraud/red flags, banking requirements, regulatory obligations, and escalation procedures?
questions.evidence: Training curriculum, attendance records, attestations, refresh schedule

questions.question: Are compliance issues, control failures, bank concerns, losses, fraud events, and regulatory findings tracked through remediation and closure?
questions.evidence: Issue log, corrective-action plans, owners/dates, closure evidence

questions.question: Has the operator documented its federal tax treatment, IRC §280E cost-of-goods-sold methodology, expense allocation approach, supporting records, and tax-advisor rationale sufficient to defend its treatment in an IRS examination?
questions.evidence: 280E memo/tax position paper, COGS allocation workpapers, tax preparer engagement letter, prior-year return support

questions.question: Can management explain cash receipts and deposits as a percentage of revenue, and reconcile that pattern to licensed locations, POS activity, METRC data, and expected peer/business activity?
questions.evidence: Cash-to-revenue ratio analysis, deposit records, METRC sales reports, peer/regional benchmark reference

questions.question: Do owners and finance personnel understand that cannabis banking commonly involves enhanced due diligence, ongoing transaction monitoring, recurring information requests, and bank-side SAR reporting consistent with applicable FinCEN guidance, and is responsibility assigned for responding accurately and promptly?
questions.evidence: Onboarding/education materials, designated bank-liaison assignment, response-time log; examples may include Marijuana Limited/Priority/Termination SAR terminology under applicable FinCEN guidance

questions.question: Has the operator prohibited or formally risk-approved payment arrangements that could disguise the underlying cannabis transaction — including cashless-ATM structures or merchant-category-code workarounds — from a financial institution or payment network?
questions.evidence: Payment-provider contracts, merchant category code documentation, internal policy prohibiting/approving disguised-transaction arrangements

questions.question: Are leases, management agreements, loans, and other transactions with owners or related entities fully disclosed, documented, and supported as bona fide, arm's-length business arrangements?
questions.evidence: Related-party lease/loan agreements, disclosure schedule, comparable-market-rate support, board/ownership approval records

instructions: Cannabis Financial Access & Compliance Readiness Assessment — Instructions

A practical diagnostic for Ohio-licensed cannabis operators to identify financial-access, control, documentation, tax-exposure, and compliance-readiness gaps before bank diligence, regulatory review, financing, or internal remediation.

Review each question with the person who owns the process. Assign a score from 0 to 3 based on the Scoring Guide. Do not score based on intention; score based on what can be demonstrated today. Put evidence, document names, owners, and remediation notes in the Notes / Evidence Found column.
0 = absent or unknown; 1 = informal/partial; 2 = documented but not consistently tested; 3 = documented, implemented, and evidenced. Higher-weight controls have greater impact on the readiness score.

Start with weight-3 controls scored 0, then other RED items, then weight-3 YELLOW items. The objective is not a perfect score; it is to identify the gaps most likely to create friction with banks, regulators, auditors, investors, or counterparties.

This tool is an operational readiness assessment, not legal advice, a legal opinion, a tax opinion, a guarantee of bank acceptance, or a determination that any specific AML, sanctions, tax, licensing, or regulatory requirement applies. Regulatory and guidance citations reflect research current as of August 27, 2026, and are provided for reference, not as a substitute for current rule text. Applicable obligations — including IRC §280E tax treatment — should be confirmed with qualified counsel, a qualified tax advisor, and relevant regulators or financial institutions.

Use the Results tab to summarize overall readiness and domain scores. Convert the highest-priority gaps into a short remediation plan with owner, target date, required evidence, and completion status.

This version includes Ohio cannabis-specific ownership and change-control references, including O.A.C. 1301:18-3-04 and 1301:18-3-06, plus cannabis banking, payment, reconciliation, related-party, and IRC §280E readiness considerations. Confirm current requirements and interpretations before relying on any cited rule or federal guidance.

Ownership-change and disclosure questions (OL-02, OL-03) are grounded in Ohio Administrative Code 1301:18-3-04 (ownership list/capitalization table disclosure, identification of 10%-or-greater owners) and 1301:18-3-06 (prior DCC approval required for ownership changes of 10% or more, aggregated per calendar year). The banking-expectations question (BF-07) references FinCEN's BSA Expectations Regarding Marijuana-Related Businesses guidance (FIN-2014-G001). Cited rules and guidance are subject to amendment or rescission — confirm current text with DCC and counsel before relying on a specific citation.
